subject: Multi-Mode MAP & evaluation checkpoints — hosting + region implications
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@aurorahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Willis <ben.willis@acmeit.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Aurora MAP kickoff - hosting modes + region sensitivity

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed by the throughput numbers and the caching examples. We agreed internally to formalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so procurement and architecture can align on a hosting mode and region path before our November review.

High level asks from Aurora:
- Confirm recommended mode for our initial POC (we have mixed latency/PHI workloads).
- Evaluate the fastest path to prod in US regions while preserving the option to move to Dedicated or Private for regulated data sets.
- Provide an itemized timeline for Eval -> Security review -> Procurement -> PO.

I've attached a MAP draft (Aurora-MAP-v2.xlsx) and our vendor security questionnaire in case you want to pre-populate answers. Can you propose a short, actionable set of checkpoints and owners we can take into our Nov 10 governance meeting?

Best,
Emily

Emily Chen
Director, Digital Platform
Aurora Health
Attachment: Aurora-MAP-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), vendor-security-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora MAP kickoff - hosting modes + region sensitivity

Hi Emily — great to kick this off. I pulled together a pragmatic MAP with clearly assigned owners and acceptance criteria; attaching our answers to the questionnaire and a one-page hosting recommendation.

Summary recommendation (POC phase):
- Start in Redwood Hosted (us-west) for fastest time-to-value and to capture performance baselines.
- For PHI-sensitive flows, ring-fence traffic via Dedicated capacity or Private VPC in a subsequent phase — we recommend a hybrid approach: Hosted for low-risk inference, Dedicated for high-throughput PHI endpoints.

Proposed checkpoints (short version):
1) Evaluation sprint (2 weeks) — perf/latency benchmark, sample KV cache hit-rate, cost-per-1k-tokens. Owner: Karthik Iyer. Acceptance: <100ms median p50 gen for 512 tokens in us-west under 50 RPS.
2) Security review (1 week parallel) — SOC2 evidence + encryption/KMS mapping. Owner: Marissa Cole. Acceptance: Questionnaire items 1-20 answered and evidence uploaded.
3) Procurement milestone (legal/price slot) — terms + reserved capacity options. Owner: Vivek Kulkarni. Acceptance: PO or signed MSA term sheet.
4) Cutover plan (2 weeks) — runbook for moving specific endpoints to Dedicated/Private, data-flow diagrams. Owner: Lauren Bishop. Acceptance: Tested canary switch and rollback plan.

Timeline recommendation: Eval kickoff 2026-11-09 -> Security/Procurement parallel work -> Target PO by 2026-11-30 -> Canary in prod for low-risk endpoints by 2026-12-14.

Attachments included: redwood-security-answers-2026.pdf, Aurora-MAP-v2-reviewed.xlsx (we annotated the MAP).

I'll let Karthik add the technical acceptance criteria below. If that looks good I can slot a 30m MAP walk-through with procurement on Tue Nov 9.

Thanks,
Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-security-answers-2026.pdf, Aurora-MAP-v2-reviewed.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@aurorahealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora MAP kickoff - hosting modes + region sensitivity

Emily, Vivek — quick technical notes to make the Eval acceptance concrete.

Technical acceptance matrix (short):
- Latency: p50 <100ms, p95 <250ms for <512 tokens in us-west under 50 RPS (as Vivek noted).
- Throughput: sustained 4.5k tokens/sec on the POC model with continuous batching enabled.
- Consistency: bitwise model variant parity between hosted and dedicated quantized variant within 0.5 ROUGE-L on our eval set.
- Data residency: any PHI payloads must be pinned to Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS; we’ll provide a VPC playbook for Aurora to validate network egress.

Operational items:
- Canary rule: initial traffic split 90% Hosted:10% Dedicated for non-PHI endpoints; evaluate latency delta over 72h.
- Cost check: we will provide a per-route cost estimate including batching and cache hit assumptions in the MAP workbook.

I’ll prepare a short runbook snippet for the Cutover plan and add a link in the shared MAP.

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@aurorahealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora MAP kickoff - hosting modes + region sensitivity

Emily — looping back with procurement cadence and asks so your legal and Sourcing teams can prepare.

Procurement checklist (items we need from Aurora):
- Standard PO or LOI indicating desired committed months/slots and approximate monthly throughput expectations.
- Counterparty contact for contracting (name + email + physical address).
- Any required amendments for data processing addendum (we can provide Redwood's DPA draft).

Suggested timeline for your governance meeting on Nov 10:
- 10m: MAP summary & proposed checkpoints (Vivek)
- 10m: Technical acceptance and canary plan (Karthik)
- 10m: Security evidence and remaining gaps (Marissa)
- 5m: Procurement next steps & PO target dates (Marissa)

If Aurora can confirm the PO contact and whether they prefer Hosted-first or Dedicated-first by EOD Nov 8, we will lock the resource planning on our side and share the detailed per-route cost estimates.

If helpful, I can also prepare a short Appendix listing upgrade paths (Hosted->Dedicated, Hosted->Private) with typical lead times and costs.

Thanks — talk soon.
Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior GTM Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: procurement-checklist-template.docx
